messages.author: c621ac38989fbf3c
messages.subject: CPO
parts:
A trickier question perhaps -
 In the models I've run the CPO values are uniformly 0 for failures. That sounds good, but is it realistic?

 I'm concerned (generally) that the models fit better where spatial data density is highest and fit more poorly where it is lower. So, I'd expect poorer performance in a cross validation measure in the low data density areas. Is it worth tacking the CPO values onto the input coordinates to see if this is true, or is this not relevant since all the points are "successes"?

Thanks,
Paul

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] CPO
parts:
The failure=0 only means that the $cpo$cpo is meaningful, that it can be computed.

You can plot the $cpo$cpo in space, yes! I usually do that.

To reiterate, what you want is the $cpo$cpo as this is the "probability of generating your datapoint from a posterior fitted without this datapoint" (i.e. the LOOCVs).

Kind regards,
Haakon
